examples.question_text:
A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x(t)$, with right positive. Write each request in function notation.

a. Find its initial displacement.
b. Find when it is at the origin.
c. Find when it is stationary.
examples.solution_text:
a. Find $x(0)$.

b. Solve $x(t)=0$ for $t$.

c. Solve $\dot{x}(t)=0$ for $t$. Stationary means zero velocity; the particle need not be at the origin.

examples.question_text:
A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x=2t^2-16t+9$, where $x$ is in metres and $t\geq0$ is in seconds. Right is positive.

a. Find its initial displacement.
b. Find its velocity and speed after $2$ seconds.
c. Find when it is stationary and its displacement then.
examples.solution_text:
a. $\begin{aligned}x(0)&=2(0)^2-16(0)+9\\&=9\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

Initially, the particle is $9\text{ m}$ right of the origin.

b. $v(t)=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4t-16$.

$\begin{aligned}v(2)&=4(2)-16\\&=-8\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

The velocity is $-8\text{ m/s}$, so the particle moves left. Its speed is $|-8|=8\text{ m/s}$.

c. Stationary means $v=0$.

$\begin{aligned}4t-16&=0\\4t&=16\\t&=4\text{ s}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}x(4)&=2(4)^2-16(4)+9\\&=-23\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

The particle is stationary after $4\text{ s}$, at $23\text{ m}$ left of the origin.

examples.question_text: A particle's displacement is $x=t^2-4t+6$, where $x$ is in metres and $t\geq0$ is in seconds. Right is positive. Find its change in displacement and total distance travelled in the first $5$ seconds.

A stone is dropped from a platform. Its height above the ground is $h=180-5t^2$, where $h$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. Upwards is positive. Find how fast it is travelling when it reaches the ground.
examples.solution_text:
At the ground, $h=0$.

$\begin{aligned}180-5t^2&=0\\5t^2&=180\\t^2&=36\\t&=6\text{ s}\end{aligned}$

Use the non-negative time.

$v(t)=\dfrac{dh}{dt}=-10t$.

$\begin{aligned}v(6)&=-10(6)\\&=-60\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

The stone moves downwards. Its impact speed is $|-60|=60\text{ m/s}$.

examples.question_text: Two particles move along the same straight line. Their displacements are $x_A=4t+7$ and $x_B=t^2+1$, measured in metres, where $t\geq0$ is in seconds. When do they have the same velocity?
examples.solution_text:
$v_A=\dfrac{dx_A}{dt}=4$ and $v_B=\dfrac{dx_B}{dt}=2t$.

For equal velocities:

$\begin{aligned}4&=2t\\t&=2\text{ s}\end{aligned}$

Their velocities are equal after $2\text{ s}$. Equal velocity does not require equal displacement.

examples.question_text: A particle moves along a straight line with displacement $x=t^2-7t+10$, where $x$ is in metres and $t\geq0$ is in seconds. Right is positive. Find when it first passes through the origin and its velocity then.
examples.solution_text:
At the origin, $x=0$.

$\begin{aligned}t^2-7t+10&=0\\(t-2)(t-5)&=0\end{aligned}$

The particle is at the origin at $t=2\text{ s}$ and $t=5\text{ s}$, so the first crossing is at $2\text{ s}$.

$v(t)=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t-7$.

$\begin{aligned}v(2)&=2(2)-7\\&=-3\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

It first passes through the origin after $2\text{ s}$, moving left at $3\text{ m/s}$.

examples.question_text: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from the ground. Its height is $x=30t-5t^2$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. Upwards is positive. Find when it returns to the ground and show that its return speed equals its initial speed.
examples.solution_text:
At the ground, $x=0$.

$\begin{aligned}30t-5t^2&=0\\5t(6-t)&=0\end{aligned}$

The ground times are $t=0$ and $t=6\text{ s}$, so the ball returns after $6\text{ s}$.

$v(t)=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=30-10t$.

$\begin{aligned}v(0)&=30\text{ m/s}\\v(6)&=30-10(6)\\&=-30\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$

The initial speed and return speed are both $30\text{ m/s}$. The velocities have opposite signs because the directions are opposite.

coverage.summary: Repaired only example 2's diagnosed diagram defect: replaced its free-form TikZ number line with a shared number-line template request and solution-only placeholder. Preserved marked positions 0, 2, 6 and 11, with jumps from 6 to 2 labelled 4 m and from 2 to 11 labelled 9 m. All other example content, extension fields and mappings are unchanged. The baseline contains no existing examples. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. Final rendering and label-size verification remain for the later visual stage.

examples.derivation: Initially means evaluate x(0); at the origin means solve x(t)=0; stationary means solve ẋ(t)=0. These match source lines 779–803.

x(0)=9 m. Differentiation gives v(t)=4t−16, so v(2)=−8 m/s and speed=8 m/s. Solving v=0 gives t=4 s; x(4)=32−64+9=−23 m. The displacement, velocity and stationary-position methods follow the supplied motion examples and exercises.

v(t)=2t−4 changes from negative to positive at t=2 s. Positions are x(0)=6 m, x(2)=2 m and x(5)=11 m. Change in displacement is 11−6=5 m; distance travelled is |2−6|+|11−2|=13 m. The solution-only shared number-line template correctly shows the journey 6→2→11 with lengths 4 m and 9 m. The method matches source Foundation Q6.
Ground contact requires 180−5t²=0, giving the physical time t=6 s. Velocity is −10t, hence impact velocity is −60 m/s and impact speed is 60 m/s. This follows source Foundation Q4.
Differentiation gives v_A=4 and v_B=2t. Equal velocities require 4=2t, giving t=2 s. Equality of displacement is unnecessary. This matches source Development Q8(b).
x=(t−2)(t−5), so origin times are 2 s and 5 s. The first is 2 s. Velocity v=2t−7 gives v(2)=−3 m/s, confirming a crossing while moving left. This matches source Foundation Q5(c–d).

x=5t(6−t) vanishes at t=0 and t=6 s, so return occurs after 6 s. Velocity v=30−10t gives initial velocity 30 m/s and return velocity −30 m/s. Both speeds are 30 m/s. This follows source Mastery Q10(b–c).
